title: Feasibility of a laboratory hold rule for early repeat HbA1c requests in primary care: a four-month pilot
abstract: Objective: to test the feasibility and safety of holding HbA1c requests made within 80 days of the previous result. Design: single-arm pilot in six practices with pre-specified progression criteria. Measures: timely overrides, safety review of held requests, firing and override rates, acceptability and second blood draws. Results will be written after the pilot.
introduction: Early repeat HbA1c testing adds little information and can prompt treatment changes within analytical variation. Hold rules reduce it elsewhere, but their safety and acceptance in primary care are uncertain.
methods: The rule held requests within 80 days and offered a coded override. Every hold and override was logged; two reviewers judged delays; requesters were surveyed at four months.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present each progression criterion with its interval estimate.
discussion: The discussion will state whether each progression criterion was met and what changes to the rule, the comment or the override route are needed. It will compare override behaviour with the retrieved reports.
limitations: Six practices over four months cannot detect rare harms, and there is no control group. Practices knew they were observed.
conclusion: To be written after the pilot. It will recommend rollout, revision or a comment-only approach against the pre-specified criteria.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility studies (non-randomised adaptation)
summary: Pilot report draft; results empty until the pilot ends.
